To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose the use of a novel hybrid discrete event/discrete time approach for the simulation of adaptive antenna systems in realistic channel conditions, and we evaluate the performance of a wireless mesh network using the proposed model.

(1) the proposed hybrid discrete-event discrete time approach is a viable way to extend the simulation of ns-2 to include adaptive antennas and realistic channel conditions; (2) the throughput of a WMN with smart antennas is significantly improved compared to the same network without smart antennas.
The proposed hybrid discrete-event discrete- time simulation approach enables the simulation of smart antennas in realistic channel condition.

the design and implementation of a hybrid simulation framework for the analysis of adaptive antennas in WMNs.
the design and development of a novel simulation tool for the performance evaluation of smart antennas in realistic wireless networks.
the development of a novel hybrid discrete-event discrete- time simulation platform that enables a more realistic modeling of adaptive antennas in wireless networks.

the developed package enables the simulation of realistic adaptive antennas in realistic wireless network environments.
